newsitem.title: UK: Italy ENEL sees lower fuel oil buying this year.
newsitem.headline: Italy ENEL sees lower fuel oil buying this year.

text.p: Italian state power utility ENEL expects its fuel oil purchases to fall by 13.7 percent in 1997, according to a report by oil industry newsletter Staffetta Quotidiana.

The utility expects to buy 19.5 million tonnes of fuel oil in 1997 against 22.6 million tonnes in 1996, the newsletter said. An Italian industry source said the figures refered to purchasing by the utility, rather than actual consumption.

The report said 4.1 million tonnes of the projected 1997 total would be high sulphur fuel oil, against five million tonnes in 1996, while 11.3 million tonnes would be low sulphur, against 13.9 million tonnes in 1996.
Some 4.1 million tonnes of the estimated 1997 total would be material with less than 0.5 percent sulphur content against 3.7 million tonnes in 1996, the report said.
Around 6.7 million tonnes was expected to come from Italy and 12.8 million tonnes from abroad.
In 1996, 6.4 million tonnes of the ultility's fuel oil consumption came from Italian suppliers and 16.2 million tonnes from abroad.
The utility's natural gas consumption was also expected to rise 2.8 percent in 1997 to 7.3 billion cubic metres (bcm) from 7.1 bcm in 1996.

An industry source estimated, however, that total Italian gas consumption would rise by more than this amount because of increased burn by independent power producers, which account for around 40 percent of Italian consumption.

Coal use was expected to drop to 7.8 million tonnes from 8.5 million tonnes in 1996, Staffeta said. The utility also expected to buy 700,000 tonnes of orimulsion in 1997, against zero consumption in 1996.
Gas oil consumption was expected to increase to 100,000 tonnes from 70,000 tonnes in 1996.
